gap: No result ChatGPT got states that its picks take three different, non-interchangeable switch sockets: the Keychron Q1 Max and K8 Max take normal-profile MX switches. The NuPhy Air75 V3 takes NuPhy's 'Low-profile 3.0' nano switches. The Lofree Flow 2 uses Kailh low-profile switches that are not pin-compatible with MX low-profile switches. A typist who wants to change switch feel later is tied to each maker's own low-profile switch line, and only the Keychrons accept the wide normal-profile MX market.
standout_why: I tried to open the two cited rival pages, RTINGS 'Best Keyboards For Typing' (rtings.com/keyboard/reviews/best/by-usage/writers) and Tom's Guide 'best mechanical keyboards'. Both returned only navigation text through the fetcher, so I could not check their article text line by line. This is a limit on my comparison. In the search results, the RTINGS single-product review of the Air75 V3 (not one of ChatGPT's results) mentions Gateron low-profile 3.0 hot-swap compatibility for that one board. I saw no page that puts the socket standards of the Keychron, NuPhy, Lofree and Logitech picks side by side. I saw none that notes Lofree's Kailh switches don't fit MX low-profile sockets. I saw none that notes VIA on the Flow 2 doesn't work over Bluetooth. Our current page says only 'hot-swap' or 'not hot-swap' in each row, without saying which switches fit.
decides: This supports the Keychron Q1 Max (and the cheaper K8 Max) as the pick for a typist who wants to try different switch feels, because both accept any normal-profile MX switch. For low-profile buyers it is a real trade-off: the Air75 V3 and Flow 2 can be hot-swapped, but replacement switches must come from NuPhy's low-profile 3.0 nano line or Lofree/Kailh's low-profile line, and the two don't cross over. Flow 2 buyers who want to remap keys need the 2.4 GHz dongle or a cable, because Gadgetoid found VIA does not work over Bluetooth.
